title: Spark pre-registers full document scaffolding for primitives it has not activated
content:
Three primitives in this chunk have their entire structure laid out — Primitive Hub Document, Active/Completed Instances Directories, In Progress Invocations Directory, Hub Data Repository with Failed Invocations and Suspended Instances subtrees — and all three read `Inactive` at their `Global Activation Status`: the Risk Capital Rental Primitive (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.2.1.1), the Asset Liability Management Rental Primitive (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.3.1.1), and the Core Governance Reward Primitive (A.6.1.1.1.2.7.1.1.1).

Every slot is empty. Not one instance exists under any of them.

This is deliberate: a single `Global Activation Status` field acts as the master switch for a primitive Spark *may* use, with all the machinery for using it already reviewed and in place. Turning a primitive on becomes a one-field change plus an Invocation, rather than a structural amendment to the Artifact negotiated under time pressure.

It also makes the Agent's option set legible. A reader can enumerate exactly which Sky Primitives Spark is entitled to invoke and which it has actually invoked, and see the difference — the Artifact documents latent capability, not just current activity. The price is that most of the Artifact's volume describes things that are not happening, which makes the document far harder to read than the operation it describes.
description: Risk Capital Rental, ALM Rental and Core Governance Reward all carry Global Activation Status Inactive yet have complete hub, directory and archive structures already built.
